clue.text: Label new kit etc.

indicators.note: new suggests these letters are made over into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: the six letters K, I, T, E, T, C are the fodder

explanation.surface: Fresh equipment and so on gets a label stuck on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal, rearranging KITETC; the full stop of the abbreviation is just punctuation.
explanation.definitionFit: A tag tied to an item, such as a price tag, is a synonym for a label.

clue.text: Spare the top man, being thoughtful

parts.note: spare can mean lean, as thin does
a king is the top man of a realm

explanation.surface: Sparing the boss is a considerate act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spare' reads as a verb (let off), but it is the adjective meaning lean.
explanation.definitionFit: Using one's mind, reflecting, is the state of being thoughtful.

clue.text: To bend about at one is good for one's health

indicators.note: about means the bend goes round the rest, enclosing it

parts.note: to curve is to bend
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Bending over is said to be beneficial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ATI inside CURVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that heals or restores, as a remedy does, benefits the body.

clue.text: Cheese found in part of dilapidated Amsterdam

indicators.note: found in part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A Dutch cheese turns up in a run-down corner of Amsterdam.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Cheese found' as the definition, but 'found' belongs to the indicator 'found in part of'; 'Cheese' alone defines. EDAM spans dilapidatED AMsterdam.
explanation.definitionFit: A round Dutch cheese with a red wax coat, an example of cheese.

clue.text: Make a song about heat in crowds

indicators.note: about means one word goes round another here, enclosing it

parts.note: to make a song is to sing
to heat something is to warm it

explanation.surface: A group sings about the heat as people throng together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts WARM inside SING, splitting it S...ING.
explanation.definitionFit: Bees or people moving in a dense mass are said to be thronging in this way.

clue.text: Making a pot-won't like to proceed carefully

indicators.note: making signals the letters are formed into something new

parts.note: the letters A, P, O, T, W, O, N, T, L, I, K, E are the fodder

explanation.surface: A potter's work that isn't liked calls for treading gently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making' signals rearranging APOTWONTLIKE; hyphen and apostrophe add nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Moving on the balls of the feet to avoid noise is an idiom for acting with great caution.

clue.text: Drops the right article in

parts.note: a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone lets fall the correct item inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the' links; 'Drops' is a noun, falling water.
explanation.definitionFit: Water falling from clouds in drops is precipitation.

clue.text: Very cold? It depends!

parts.note: depends is read literally as hangs down, of something frozen hanging from a gutter

explanation.surface: Asked whether it is freezing, someone hedges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It depends' sounds like an evasive reply, but depend once meant hang down.
explanation.definitionFit: A hanging spike of frozen water, formed by dripping, is freezing and dangles.

clue.text: Fish swallowing the cockle

indicators.note: swallowing means the fish takes the other word inside it

parts.note: a gar is a long-snouted fish

explanation.surface: A fish gulps down a shellfish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cockle' looks like the shellfish but is the verb meaning pucker or wrinkle, as fabric does.
explanation.definitionFit: To pucker cloth into folds is to draw it in, a sewing sense of cockle.

clue.text: An encroachment on the fashionable way

parts.note: in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'
a road is a way

explanation.surface: A trendy route is said to trespass on someone's ground.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a gain into enemy territory or someone's domain is an advance or encroachment.

clue.text: It's plain stupid for a mountaineer

indicators.note: stupid suggests the letters have been put together senselessly, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters I, T, S, P, L, A, I, N are the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone declares it's obviously foolish to be a climber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stupid' signals rearranging ITSPLAIN; the apostrophe adds no letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A climber of high peaks, originally of the Alps, is a synonym for mountaineer.

clue.text: People trained in a down-to-earth way

definitions.text: People trained in a down-to-earth way

parts.words: People trained in a down-to-earth way
parts.note: down-to-earth is read literally, as travelling downwards to the ground through the air

explanation.surface: Folk taught to be practical and sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'down-to-earth' suggests practicality; literally it is descending to land under a canopy.
explanation.definitionFit: Jumpers taught to drop from aircraft under a canopy descend to the ground.

clue.text: Children may get a line on this bird

definitions.text: Children may get a line on this

explanation.surface: Youngsters might be able to string up a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A toy flown by children on a string, and also a fork-tailed hawk: one word for both.

clue.text: The domestic fowl is obviously covered

explanation.surface: A farmyard bird is plainly kept under wraps.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits the answer as CAP ON: wearing a hat, so plainly covered.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated cockerel fattened for eating; and split in two, wearing a hat, hence covered.

clue.text: Light rod-about a pound

indicators.note: about means the rod goes round the other piece, enclosing it

parts.note: a cue is the rod used in snooker or billiards
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: A lightweight stick weighs roughly a pound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Light' looks like an adjective meaning not heavy; here it is a noun, something that sheds light on a problem.
explanation.definitionFit: A hint that sheds light on a mystery is a pointer or helpful lead.

clue.text: To expose about fifty would be sound

indicators.note: about means the exposing word goes round the fifty, enclosing it

parts.note: to bare something is to expose it
L is the Roman numeral fifty

explanation.surface: Revealing roughly fifty is considered sensible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'would be' links; 'sound' looks like an adjective (sensible) but is a noun, a loud noise.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud harsh noise, as of trumpets, is one kind of sound.

clue.text: A revolting individual

parts.note: revolting is read as rising up against authority, not as disgusting

explanation.surface: A disgusting person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who rises against a ruler or government is an insurgent.

clue.text: Engagements in the main

parts.note: engagements read as fights rather than betrothals, and the main is old poetic language for the open sea

explanation.surface: Commitments that are mostly social, or the main ones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the main' reads as 'mostly', but 'the main' is the sea, and engagements are fights.
explanation.definitionFit: Fights between fleets of warships at sea are engagements on the ocean.

clue.text: Back up the big family and there's strong criticism

indicators.note: up in a down clue says the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to back someone is to aid them
a tribe is a large family group or clan

explanation.surface: Support the large clan, and there's harsh censure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back up' looks like one phrase meaning support; 'Back' gives AID and 'up' turns it to DIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A bitter verbal attack or tirade is a piece of harsh criticism.

clue.text: Most austere holy men keep a bird

indicators.note: keep means the holy men hold the bird inside

parts.note: two saints, each abbreviated St
an erne is a sea eagle

explanation.surface: Strict monks look after a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keep' puts ERNE between ST and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: Severest or harshest, the superlative of stern, means most austere.

clue.text: The poor staid ill-used surgeon

indicators.note: ill-used means treated badly, so these letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: the twelve letters of these three words are the fodder

explanation.surface: A poor, sober doctor has been badly treated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-used' signals rearranging THEPOORSTAID.
explanation.definitionFit: A specialist operating on bones and joints is one kind of surgeon.

clue.text: Timid guy setting a crowd at odds

indicators.note: at odds suggests the letters are in disagreement, so out of order

explanation.surface: A nervous man upsets a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at odds' signals rearranging ACROWD; 'setting' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A man lacking courage, a craven or poltroon.

clue.text: Call for a comedian!

explanation.surface: Someone phones to book a comic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud cry or shriek is a call; and a hilarious person is informally said to be one.

clue.text: Not now applied to cigarette ends

parts.note: a plaster applied to a cut is on it

indicators.note: ends asks for the first and last letters of the word cigarette

explanation.surface: Not at the moment, said of the stubs of cigarettes.
explanation.definitionFit: Formerly, at some past time, so not at present.

clue.text: One point over 500 will be tolerated

parts.note: S is south, one point of the compass
over can mean excessively, as too does in 'too much'
D is the Roman numeral for five hundred

explanation.surface: A single point beyond five hundred will be accepted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will be' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To have put up with something, endured or borne it, is to have tolerated it.

clue.text: Agitate for porridge

explanation.surface: A cook is told to mix the oatmeal.
explanation.walkthrough: Porridge is British slang for a prison sentence; stir is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: To mix or shake up is to agitate; and slang for jail, as porridge is slang for time inside.

clue.text: Money that's taken in after some business

indicators.note: taken in after says the word in comes after the business abbreviation

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company, a business

explanation.surface: Cash taken in after some trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' and 'that's taken' link.
explanation.definitionFit: A metal disc used as currency is a piece of money.

clue.text: Inferior ground

explanation.surface: A lowly patch of earth.
explanation.definitionFit: Low or mean in quality or morals; and the foundation or bottom on which something rests.

clue.text: The pub appears a dreadful hole with wear and tear

indicators.note: dreadful suggests the letters are in a terrible state and need rearranging

parts.note: taken as written
use is the wear and tear an object suffers

explanation.surface: The bar looks an awful dump, showing much wear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' signals rearranging AHOLE to ALEHO.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a tavern where beer is served, a synonym for a pub.

clue.text: Parasites follow a well-qualified person for spite

indicators.note: follow means the parasites come after the other piece

parts.note: an MA, a Master of Arts, is a graduate with a higher degree
lice are parasites

explanation.surface: Bugs pursue a scholar out of nastiness.
explanation.definitionFit: Ill will or a desire to harm is a synonym for spite.

clue.text: Reduce by taking food with little in it

indicators.note: with little in it says the small piece goes inside the food

parts.note: a dish is food served at a meal
mini means little

explanation.surface: Eat food with not much in it to cut down.
explanation.definitionFit: To make smaller or lessen is a synonym for reduce.

clue.text: Rue crack about exercise

indicators.note: about means the crack goes round the exercise, enclosing it

parts.note: a rent is a tear or crack
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: Someone regrets a split around gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: To feel sorry for a wrong done is to regret it, a synonym for rue.
